# SL₂ is generated by its upper and lower additive roots

The theorem `Langlands.GroupScheme.specialLinearBinaryRootGeneration.{u}` proves exactly
`Langlands.GroupScheme.SpecialLinearBinaryRootGenerationStatement.{u}`. It imports the
published statement without changing that statement or its dependencies. The result holds
for every field in every universe, including fields of characteristic two, and adds no
hypotheses.

## Target and provenance

The target is the Library's scheme-theoretic version of Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017),
Proposition 20.23, printed p. 415, with proof on p. 416. Its precise source correspondence
and the two actual root morphisms are documented in
[the published statement](SpecialLinearBinaryRootGenerationStatement.md). The source is
registered as `milne-2017-algebraic-groups`, SHA-256
`899b0f44f3c3ccfbaf5ed1cf9c180be7a8016b1c0e9709ca0c206304e5bd1cd0`.

The proof below is a derived algebraic proof, rather than Milne's Lie-algebra proof. It
uses the transvection induction already used in the Library's rational generation result
in [SpecialLinearBinaryRootGroups](SpecialLinearBinaryRootGroups.md), and applies it to
all residue fields. It then uses reducedness to recover the scheme structure.
The two private lemmas are internal consequences of existing point equivalences and
Mathlib's matrix and scheme APIs; they make no additional mathematical assumptions.

## Implemented proof

Fix a field `k`, and let `q : H ⟶ SL₂` be an arbitrary closed subgroup through which both
root morphisms factor. Here a factorization is a morphism of relative schemes as in
`FactorsThrough`, and the required conclusion is containment of image subgroup functors
on every test scheme.

First, `SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.mem_range_of_field_sections` treats any relative test
scheme `T` whose ring of global sections is a field. The existing multiplicative
equivalence `SpecialLinear.pointsEquiv` identifies `SL₂(T)` with determinant-one matrices
over that ring. For every coefficient `a`, the inverse of `VectorGroup.coordinates`
produces an additive-root point with constant coordinate `a`. The formula
`pointsEquiv_rootMap` identifies its image with the corresponding transvection. The two
factorizations through `q` therefore put both kinds of transvections in the subgroup
`(SubgroupFunctor.range q).carrier T`. Splitting the two matrix indices exhausts all
off-diagonal transvections. The subgroup is closed under multiplication, so
`Matrix.SL2.transvection_induction` puts every determinant-one matrix, hence every
`T`-point, in that range. An explicit `IsField` assumption and its local `toField`
structure preserve the existing ring operations of the section ring.

Second, `SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.surjective_of_root_factors` applies this argument to
each underlying point `x` of `SL₂`. It equips the spectrum of the residue field at `x`
with the composite structure map to the base, and uses the canonical morphism
`fromSpecResidueField x` as its `SL₂`-point. The isomorphism `Scheme.ΓSpecIso` makes its
ring of global sections a field, so the first lemma factors this morphism through `q`.
Evaluating the factorization at the unique point of the residue-field spectrum gives a
preimage of `x`, by `Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply`. Thus the underlying scheme
morphism of `q` is surjective. This step needs neither a closedness assumption on `q`
nor a field assumption on the original base ring.

Finally, the main theorem uses `SpecialLinear.smooth_groupScheme` and
`SmoothReducedProof.isReduced_of_smooth_over_field` to show that `SL₂` is reduced.
The competitor `q` is a surjective closed immersion into this reduced target, so
`isIso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_surjective` makes its underlying scheme morphism an
isomorphism. Reflection by `Over.forget` gives an isomorphism of relative schemes.
On any relative test scheme, composing an arbitrary `SL₂`-point with its inverse
explicitly lifts that point to `H`. This proves the required containment on every test
scheme, including nonreduced test schemes. The identity of `SL₂` is itself a closed
immersion, and both root maps factor through it by the identity law, giving the other
two clauses of `IsGeneratedByFamily`.

## Verification

The proof module and the exact theorem were checked with the project's pinned Lean
environment. The theorem has the sole universe parameter `u`; its only logical axioms
are `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Compilation and inspection had no
errors or warnings. Independent review and the submission's build and exact-target
checks determine formal acceptance.
